kid.question: What did Darius tell people to do toward Daniel's God?

options.text: Tremble and fear before Him
Offer daily gifts at Jerusalem
Sing His praises each morning
Pray facing the royal palace

kid.explanation: Darius's decree calls for reverence before Daniel's living, steadfast God, who delivers and rescues.

kid.question: What does Darius say about God's kingdom?

options.text: It will last thirty days
It will pass to Babylon
It will not be destroyed
It will divide among governors

kid.explanation: The proclamation describes God's kingdom as indestructible and His dominion as enduring to the end.

kid.question: What did Daniel do with his own dream?

options.text: He kept it unwritten
He erased its record
He wrote it down
He sent it to Egypt

kid.explanation: Daniel wrote the dream and told the sum of its matters.

kid.question: Where did the four great beasts come from?

options.text: The great sea
The royal garden
The dry valley
The temple courtyard

kid.explanation: After the four winds strive upon the sea, four different beasts come up from it.

kid.question: What change happened to the first beast?

options.text: It flew like an eagle and received a bird's voice
It stood like a man and received a man's heart
It ran like a horse and received a lion's tail
It swam like a fish and received a serpent's head

kid.explanation: The lion-like beast loses its eagle wings, stands like a man, and receives a man's heart.

kid.question: What unusual features did the leopard-like beast have?

options.text: Two wings and seven heads
Four wings and four heads
Eight wings and three heads
Six wings and two heads

kid.explanation: Daniel describes a leopard-like beast with four bird wings and four heads, to which dominion is given.

kid.question: What happened when the heavenly judgment was set?

options.text: The clouds were scattered
The sea was emptied
The stars were hidden
The books were opened

kid.explanation: The Ancient of days sits amid a vast heavenly assembly; the judgment is set and books are opened.

kid.question: Who came with the clouds of heaven?

options.text: One like the captain of guards
One like the Son of man
One like the king of Babylon
One like the priest of Judah

kid.explanation: Daniel sees one like the Son of man come with heaven's clouds and approach the Ancient of days.

kid.question: What did Daniel learn that the four beasts represented?

options.text: Four kings arising from the earth
Four priests guarding the temple
Four captains protecting the palace
Four rivers crossing the kingdom

kid.explanation: The interpreter tells Daniel that the four great beasts are four kings that will arise out of the earth.

kid.question: What happened after the horn fought against the saints?

options.text: The saints fled and the horn kept the kingdom
Judgment ended and the horn received another kingdom
The saints surrendered and appointed the horn their king
Judgment came and the saints received the kingdom

kid.explanation: The horn prevails against the saints until the Ancient of days comes and the time arrives for the saints to possess the kingdom.

high-school.question: What does Darius's proclamation emphasize about Daniel's God?

options.text: Local sovereignty restricted to Judean religious ceremonies
Enduring sovereignty expressed in rescue and signs
Temporary sovereignty assigned by the Median royal court
Hidden sovereignty awaiting recognition by Babylon's priests

high-school.explanation: Darius calls Him living and steadfast, with indestructible dominion, and credits Him with rescuing Daniel and working signs.

high-school.question: How does the account introduce Daniel's vision?

options.text: He receives a written decree describing armies outside a city
He follows a daytime guide through a temple filled with animals
He records a night dream of differing beasts from a stirred sea
He explains a royal dream of matching statues beside a river

high-school.explanation: Daniel dates and records his own dream, then describes winds striving upon the sea and four diverse beasts emerging.

high-school.question: How do the first three beasts differ in their portrayals?

options.text: A crowned lion, a crouching bear, and a leopard with iron teeth
A transformed lion, a raised bear, and a winged multi-headed leopard
A speaking lion, a winged bear, and a leopard carrying three ribs
A horned lion, a wounded bear, and a leopard with human eyes

high-school.explanation: The lion is transformed, the bear raised on one side with ribs in its mouth, and the leopard has four wings and heads.

high-school.question: What makes the fourth beast's description especially threatening?

options.text: Its crushing violence is joined by horns and a boastful new horn
Its devouring mouth is joined by wings and a blood-covered crown
Its tearing claws are joined by ribs and a commanding human voice
Its trampling feet are joined by heads and a weapon-bearing human arm

high-school.explanation: The beast devours, crushes, and tramples; the little horn uproots three horns and speaks great things.

high-school.question: What change follows the boastful beast scene?

options.text: Heavenly judgment restores the beasts' power over every nation
Heavenly judgment returns the opened books to Babylon's rulers
Heavenly judgment removes beastly power and destroys the beast
Heavenly judgment appoints the little horn to govern the assembly

high-school.explanation: The Ancient of days sits, judgment is set, and the boastful beast is destroyed while the other beasts lose dominion.

high-school.question: What is the scope of the Son of man's received authority?

options.text: The heavenly messengers serve His authority while earthly kingdoms remain separate
The four beasts serve His authority until the little horn returns
The people of Babylon serve His authority for one royal lifetime
All peoples, nations, and languages serve His enduring dominion

high-school.explanation: He receives dominion, glory, and a kingdom for all peoples, nations, and languages, with no passing away or destruction.

high-school.question: How does Daniel respond to being troubled by the vision?

options.text: He asks a nearby figure and receives an interpretation
He destroys his written account and refuses further questions
He summons the king and asks for another royal reward
He gathers his companions and asks them to choose a ruler

high-school.explanation: Daniel approaches one standing by and asks the truth; the figure explains the beasts and the saints' eventual possession.

high-school.question: Which subject does Daniel pursue after the initial interpretation?

options.text: The different fourth beast and the horn warring against the saints
The first beast's human heart and its return to the stirred sea
The second beast's raised side and the location of its royal capital
The third beast's four heads and its appointment over the heavenly court

high-school.explanation: Daniel stresses its distinctiveness, destructive power, horns, and the horn's successful war against the saints before judgment.

high-school.question: How does the horn's authority compare with the final kingdom?

options.text: Its oppression is everlasting; the saints' kingdom lasts one season
Its oppression is bounded; the saints' kingdom is everlasting
Its oppression is symbolic; the saints' kingdom remains under its laws
Its oppression is voluntary; the saints' kingdom depends on its permission

high-school.explanation: The horn's period is limited, judgment removes its dominion, and an everlasting kingdom is given to the saints.

high-school.question: How does Daniel end his account of the vision?

options.text: He becomes angry and demands the interpreter change the message
He becomes king and publishes the matter as royal law
He becomes carefree and dismisses the matter from his mind
He remains troubled and keeps the matter in his heart

high-school.explanation: His thoughts still trouble him and his appearance changes, but he keeps the matter in his heart.

expert.question: What continuity joins Darius's proclamation and the Son of man scene?

options.text: Indestructible dominion connects Darius's account of rescue with the Son of man's kingship
Temporary dominion connects Darius's account of rescue with the little horn's final victory
Provincial dominion connects Darius's account of rescue with four permanent rival kingdoms
Inherited dominion connects Darius's account of rescue with Babylon's restored royal dynasty

expert.explanation: Darius describes God's indestructible kingdom; the Son of man receives an everlasting dominion and indestructible kingdom in the vision.

expert.question: Which contrast distinguishes the first beast's transformation from the little horn's emergence?

options.text: The first receives human names and offices; the horn bears human wings and flies
The first receives human stance and heart; the horn bears human eyes and boasts
The first receives human speech and law; the horn bears human hands and serves
The first receives human clothing and books; the horn bears human feet and kneels

expert.explanation: The lion-like beast stands as a man with a man's heart; the little horn has human-like eyes and a mouth speaking great things.

expert.question: Which details characterize the assembly in Daniel 7:9-10?

options.text: A standing Son of man, a divided sea, four attendants, and sealed books
A seated Ancient of days, a fiery stream, vast attendants, and opened books
A seated earthly king, a golden throne, ten attendants, and royal decrees
A standing heavenly watcher, a fallen tree, seven attendants, and iron bands

expert.explanation: The Ancient of days sits with vast attendants; judgment is set and the books opened, shifting the scene to heavenly adjudication.

expert.question: What distinction is made between the beast's fate and the others' fate?

options.text: The beast keeps dominion; the others are immediately destroyed by fire
The beast receives a kingdom; the others become servants of its new horn
The beast loses its horns; the others recover their earlier dominion forever
The beast is destroyed; the others lose dominion but live for a season

expert.explanation: The beast's body is destroyed and given to fire; the rest lose dominion while their lives are prolonged for a season and time.

expert.question: What relationship is depicted between the Son of man and the Ancient of days?

options.text: The Son of man hides and delegates dominion to the horn before judgment
The Son of man withdraws and returns dominion to the four earthly beasts
The Son of man contends and seizes dominion from the seated heavenly judge
The Son of man approaches and is given dominion, glory, and kingdom

expert.explanation: The Son of man comes to the Ancient of days and is brought near; dominion, glory, and a kingdom are given to Him.

expert.question: What contrast governs the interpreter's first summary?

options.text: Four earthly kingdoms unite, but the saints inherit a separate temporary realm
Four earthly kings arise, but the saints possess the kingdom forever
Four heavenly messengers speak, but the horn determines the saints' final rulers
Four heavenly judges descend, but the beasts preserve their dominion forever

expert.explanation: The beasts are four kings arising from the earth; the summary immediately contrasts this with the saints' everlasting possession.

expert.question: How does the vision prevent treating the horn's success as the final outcome?

options.text: Its victory lasts until judgment and the saints' possession arrive
Its victory lasts until the saints accept the horn's revised laws
Its victory lasts until Daniel abandons his request for interpretation
Its victory lasts until the beasts elect a different earthly ruler

expert.explanation: The horn makes war and prevails, but the stated 'until' introduces the Ancient of days, judgment, and the saints' possession.

expert.question: How does the interpretation develop the little horn's political and religious activity?

options.text: A later king replaces ten, opens the books, and transfers judgment to the saints
A later king crowns three, instructs the saints, and preserves their appointed times
A later king subdues three, opposes the Most High, and seeks altered times and laws
A later king unites ten, serves the Most High, and restores the earlier royal laws

expert.explanation: The later ruler subdues three kings, speaks against the Most High, wears out the saints, and thinks to change times and laws before judgment removes his power.

expert.question: What shift in setting marks the move from Daniel 6:28 to 7:1?

options.text: Prosperity under Darius and Cyrus gives way to a dream dated under Belshazzar
Prosperity under Belshazzar and Cyrus gives way to a dream dated under Darius
A dream under Darius and Belshazzar gives way to prosperity dated under Cyrus
A dream under Cyrus and Belshazzar gives way to prosperity dated under Darius

expert.explanation: Daniel 6 closes by naming Darius and Cyrus in the account of his prosperity. Daniel 7 opens by dating his dream to Belshazzar's first year.

expert.question: How does Daniel's final reaction qualify the effect of receiving an interpretation?

options.text: Receiving the explanation leaves Daniel free from distress and ready for royal office
Receiving the explanation leads Daniel to discard his record and forget the vision
Receiving the explanation leaves Daniel with troubling thoughts and a changed countenance
Receiving the explanation leads Daniel to conceal the outcome from his own memory

expert.explanation: He seeks and receives an interpretation, but the ending still describes troubling thoughts and a changed countenance, with the matter kept in his heart.
